Evidence & scope

Scoped methods, data-collection or experiment claims were read from the exact pinned preprint version by separate author, source-verifier and adversarial AI invocations. The full cited contexts, including conditions and model/table identities, are bound to approved observations; actual partial/full/unread scopes are retained in review records. This is not a complete-paper, latest-version, corpus, proof, labor, supplier-performance or experiment-reproduction audit. Work and version remain distinct and contribute at most one reviewed paper work.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The Problems with Proxies: Making Data Work Visible through Requester Practices (2408.11667v1) · paper method: The authors distinguish proxies for worker identity/suitability from proxies for ability to produce desired data, observing combined filtering in requester accounts.

cohort8.claim.proxies.proxy-types

  • Original author-stage note: Author-only candidate: separate source-verifier and adversarial source-content reviews remain pending.
  • Version-specific primary-source report. Proofs, model experiments, underlying data, consent/pay records and supplier participation have not been independently reproduced or audited.
  • Qualitative thematic finding in this US requester sample; no prevalence estimate or global ranking of platforms is asserted.

The Problems with Proxies: Making Data Work Visible through Requester Practices (2408.11667v1) · paper method: The study interviews 52 requesters from academic and industry settings between November 2022 and January 2023.

The Problems with Proxies: Making Data Work Visible through Requester Practices (2408.11667v1) · paper method: The paper limits its findings to US requester perspectives and warns that reported experiences may differ from behavior in practice.
